# Results — Study 39 (Black-Box) on real cryptocurrencies

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Daily closes for
**BTC-USD, ETH-USD, LTC-USD, XRP-USD** from Yahoo! Finance, 2017–2026, cached to
`_cache/black_box_crypto.parquet`. The strategy is a small **`MLPClassifier`** (hidden layers
(32, 16), fixed `random_state`) fed a causal, strictly-lagged feature bank (last 5 returns, 5- and
10-day momentum, 10-day realised vol, a 10-day z-score) and asked to predict the **sign of the next
day's return**; it trades the predicted sign. Two evaluation modes: **in-sample** (fit and predict on the
same tape — the trap) and **walk-forward** (2-year initial train, ~6-month out-of-sample blocks,
expanding). The offline core proves the apparatus on a synthetic series with a known weak nonlinear
signal (positive control) and a random-walk null. As-of **2026-06-10**; match the fingerprint below.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` (out-of-sample) · Tradability `MIRAGE` · Overfit? `CONFIRMED`

This is the machine-learning counterpart to [Study 22 (Crystal-Ball)](../../22-crystal-ball/), and the
lesson is the same: a backtest can be a mirage. Fit-and-scored on the **same** data, the MLP looks like a
money printer — on BTC, an in-sample Sharpe of **5.38** at **66%** directional accuracy. But that number
is bookkeeping, not forecasting: the net has already seen every label it is "predicting." The only number
a live trader could have earned is the **walk-forward** one, and there the edge evaporates — a gross OOS
Sharpe of **0.90** but at **51.2%** accuracy (a coin-flip), and that small gross number is just the net's
long bias riding crypto's secular bull, not directional skill. Across all four coins the out-of-sample
gross Sharpe is small and inconsistent (BTC +0.90, ETH +0.41, LTC +0.34, XRP +0.32) with accuracy
pinned near **0.51** everywhere; net of realistic crypto costs it is negative (BTC −0.18 at 20 bp; ETH
already −0.01 at 10 bp). And the in-sample number is provably overfitting: when we randomly **shuffle the
labels** — destroying any real relationship — the net still reproduces them in-sample with **66–69%**
training accuracy, essentially identical to the **66.4%** on the true labels. It was memorising noise all
along.

## Data stamp

- **Coins**: BTC-USD, ETH-USD, LTC-USD, XRP-USD — daily closes, 2017-01-01 → 2026-06-10, 3448 days,
  inputs fingerprint `b90e60f0ace7`
- **As-of**: 2026-06-10 (slice frozen so reruns don't drift)

## In-sample vs walk-forward out-of-sample (BTC flagship)

| evaluation | Sharpe (gross) | accuracy | Sharpe (net @10 bp) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **in-sample (the trap)** | **5.38** | **0.664** | — |
| **walk-forward (honest)** | 0.90 | 0.512 | 0.36 |

The in-sample Sharpe is **5.38** at **66.4%** accuracy; the honest walk-forward Sharpe is **0.90** at
**51.2%** accuracy (≈ a coin-flip). The entire apparent edge is the gap between the two — the textbook
signature of an over-parameterised learner memorising in-sample noise. The small *gross* OOS Sharpe is a
long-bias artefact (the net mostly stays long and BTC trended up over the window); it is not directional
skill, as the 0.512 accuracy and the cost wall below make plain.

## Across the coins (walk-forward OOS Sharpe)

| coin | in-sample Sharpe | OOS Sharpe | OOS accuracy | net @10 bp | break-even |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BTC-USD | 5.38 | +0.90 | 0.512 | +0.36 | 16.7 bp |
| ETH-USD | 5.43 | +0.41 | 0.518 | −0.01 | 9.7 bp |
| LTC-USD | 4.66 | +0.34 | 0.516 | −0.09 | 8.0 bp |
| XRP-USD | 4.74 | +0.32 | 0.512 | −0.02 | 9.3 bp |

In-sample every coin scores a Sharpe near 5 at ~66% accuracy; out-of-sample every coin sits at ~0.51
accuracy — a coin-flip — and only BTC keeps a (long-bias) positive net Sharpe at the gentlest cost. No
coin shows a consistent, directional, cost-surviving out-of-sample edge. `NONE`.

## The cost wall (BTC OOS book)

| cost (bp/unit) | 0 | 5 | 10 | 20 | 50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| net OOS Sharpe | 0.897 | 0.628 | 0.359 | −0.178 | −1.772 |

There is essentially no gross out-of-sample edge for costs to erode; the book flips position often, so
realistic crypto round-trip costs (10–20 bp+) push any noise-sized Sharpe firmly negative. `MIRAGE`.

## The overfitting proof — shuffled-label control (BTC, in-sample)

In-sample **training accuracy**, true labels vs randomly shuffled labels (4 shuffles): true **0.664**
vs shuffled **0.662, 0.668, 0.687, 0.668**. The net reproduces *meaningless* labels in-sample exactly as
well as the real ones — so the gorgeous in-sample number measures the net's capacity to fit whatever it is
handed, not predictive skill. `CONFIRMED`. Detail in [`extension.md`](extension.md).
